name: MN-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: District carries an 18-point Republican partisan lean, one of the reddest in Minnesota
Fischbach holds a roughly 4-to-1 fundraising advantage ($1.29M raised, $920K on hand vs. $335K for Osberg)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
No public polls or expert ratings; a Democratic-tilted national environment is the main counterweight
model.rationale: An 18-point Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and market odds near 4% for Democrats all point to a comfortable Fischbach re-election; only the favorable national environment for Democrats and Osberg's modest but real fundraising keep the margin from being wider.
model.watch: A wave-scale national shift against Republicans or an unexpected scandal involving Fischbach could narrow the race, but no current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
MN-07 spans rural western Minnesota and carries an 18-point Republican partisan lean, among the reddest districts in the state. Incumbent Michelle Fischbach is seeking re-election with about $1.3 million raised and $920,000 in cash on hand. Democratic challenger Erik Osberg has raised roughly $335,000. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance of winning.

Fundamentals point clearly toward a Republican hold: the district lean, incumbency, and a large money advantage all favor Fischbach. A national environment tilted toward Democrats and Osberg's nontrivial fundraising are the main reasons a somewhat closer result cannot be ruled out, but nothing in the available evidence suggests the seat is genuinely in play.
